question: Which is the oldest Stupa of the Buddhist Period?
solution:
The correct answer is **Sanchi Stupa**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sanchi Stupa** is one of the oldest stone structures in India and was originally commissioned by Emperor Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE.
 
• This stupa is a central part of the Buddhist architecture and serves as a significant monument for the followers of Buddhism.
 
• The stupa consists of a hemispherical dome containing relics of the Buddha.
 
• It has been a UNESCO World Heritage site since 1989.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
 

 Option
 Details
 
 

 Option 1: Dhamek Stupa
 Located in Sarnath, Uttar Pradesh, it marks the spot where Buddha gave his first sermon.
 
 

 Option 2: Mahabodhi Stupa
 Located in Bodh Gaya, Bihar, it commemorates the enlightenment of Buddha.
 
 

 Option 3: Kesariya Stupa
 Located in Bihar, it is one of the tallest and largest Buddhist stupas in the world.
